Gynecology and urology · published research

Mammary implant pseudocapsules

In one rat implant model, laser treatment reduced pseudocapsule thickness and implant pressure, with the pressure difference significant at 180 days. Most histologic features were similar between groups.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In one rat implant model, laser treatment reduced pseudocapsule thickness and implant pressure, with the pressure difference significant at 180 days. Most histologic features were similar between groups.

Summary of the Evidence

One controlled experiment studied 60 male Wistar rats with smooth silicone implants placed under the skin on the back. This is a preclinical foreign-body model, not a study of women with breast implants. No human trial or duplicate publication was identified.

Human and clinical evidence

No clinical study was identified for breast-implant pseudocapsules or capsular contracture. Outcomes such as pain, implant distortion, Baker grade, repeat surgery, and recurrence therefore remain untested in people.

Animal evidence

Laser-treated rats had thinner pseudocapsules than untreated rats at the measured time points. Implant pressure was lower in the treated group at 180 days. The cellularity and collagen pattern were otherwise similar between groups, although enlarged blood vessels were more frequent after treatment. Thus, the study found directional changes in capsule thickness and pressure without showing a broad change in the tissue reaction (Palhares et al. 2009; full text).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No separate cell-culture or ex-vivo study of implant pseudocapsule formation was identified.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

The rat implants were irradiated over four points with continuous 780-nm near-infrared light. Each point received 1 J/cm² per pulse, in seven sessions given every other day over 14 days. The first session followed surgery immediately. These exposure details belong to this specific rat protocol; no comparison tested another wavelength, dose, schedule, implant surface, or placement.

Interpretation

The study supports reduced capsule thickness and pressure in its rat model, while the similar histology limits claims about a general anti-inflammatory effect. Dorsal subcutaneous implants in male rats do not reproduce breast anatomy, implant positioning, or clinical contracture outcomes. The findings are a reason to test the model and outcomes further, not evidence that PBM prevents or treats capsular contracture in patients.

Evidence strength in source summaryVery low for reducing pseudocapsule thickness and implant pressure in rats
Publications and records1 article

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

One controlled rat experiment found thinner pseudocapsules and lower pressure around silicone implants after laser treatment, while most tissue features were similar. This supports an effect within that model, not proven prevention of human capsular contracture. Replication in a model closer to breast implantation, followed by controlled patient studies measuring symptoms and revision surgery, would be needed to strengthen the conclusion.
